title: What Is a Game?
meaning:
What is a game?
A game is a structured play, typically for entertainment or education, with rules, goals,
and interaction.
Components: players, rules, objectives, feedback system, voluntary participation.
Why it matters: Games are rapidly grown as a medium
beyond entertainment (education, training, simulation).

title: What Is Gamification?
meaning:
What is Gamification?
What is Gamification?
The application of game-design elements
(points, badges, leaderboards, challenges) in non-game contexts.
Why use it: Boosts engagement, motivation, behaviour change.
Illustrative industries:
Corporate training (e.g., sales reps rewarded for modules completed)
E-learning / education (students gaining badges for tasks)
Health & wellness apps (fitness challenges)
Marketing/retail (loyalty programmes with “levels”)
Insurance Sector (to create simulations and risk assessments)
Finance (Example: trading apps/ crypto exchanges etc.)

title: What Is Game Testing?
meaning:
What is Game Testing?
Game testing is a structured quality assurance process that evaluates
video games to identify bugs, ensure functionality, and verify the
player experience meets quality standards before release.
It's more than just playing games—it's a methodical approach to
finding issues, documenting them clearly, and helping developers
create polished, engaging experiences that players love.

title: Becoming a Professional Game Tester
summary: Session 1 ? Becoming a Professional Game Tester
meaning:
How One Can Become a Professional Game Tester?
Prerequisites / Skills:
Strong attention to detail & curiosity (find bugs, break
things)
Basic technical awareness: familiarity with platforms
(mobile, PC, console), ability to reproduce issues,
understanding resolution/performance/compatibility
concepts.
Communication skills: to write bug reports clearly, work
in teams.
Domain knowledge: gaming mechanics, user behaviour,
UX.
(Preferred) Some programming / scripting / test
automation basics for advanced roles.
Qualifications & Certifications:
Formal education: e.g., degree in computer science/IT or
game design/QA is helpful but not always mandatory.
Certifications/training: Courses on game testing,
software QA, gamification, etc.
Portfolio: Having played, tested games, contributed bug
logs (internships, volunteer).

title: Why QA Matters in Gaming
summary: Session 1 ? Why QA Matters in Gaming
meaning:
Why QA Matters in Gaming
Player Experience
Quality testing ensures smooth, enjoyable gameplay
that keeps players engaged and satisfied from start to
finish.
Brand Reputation
Polished releases build trust and loyalty. Buggy
launches damage studio credibility and player
confidence.
Cost Savings
Finding bugs early is exponentially cheaper than post-
launch fixes, patches, and customer support.
Smoother Development
QA feedback helps teams iterate faster, make informed
decisions, and deliver on schedule with confidence.

title: QA in the Game Development Pipeline
summary: Session 1 ? QA in the Game Development Pipeline
meaning:
QA in the Game Development
Pipeline
Quality assurance isn't just a final checkpoint—it's integrated throughout the entire
development cycle. QA testers work alongside designers, artists, and programmers from
pre-production through post-launch support.
Pre-Production
Planning test strategies and understanding game vision
Production
Continuous testing as features are built and integrated
Launch & Beyond
Final verification and post-release monitoring
Early detection is invaluable: Catching issues during development prevents them from
becoming expensive, time-consuming problems later. A bug found in alpha testing might
take hours to fix; the same bug discovered after launch could cost thousands in patches
and lost players.

title: Types of Game Testing
meaning:
Types of Game Testing
Game testing encompasses multiple specialized areas, each focusing on different aspects of quality and player experience.
Here are the core testing types every game tester should understand:
1
Functional Testing
Verifies that game features, mechanics, and systems
work as intended without errors or crashes.
2
UI/UX Testing
Evaluates interface design, navigation flow, readability,
and overall user experience quality.
3
Playtesting
Assesses fun factor, game balance, pacing, difficulty
curves, and player engagement levels.
4
Compatibility Testing
Ensures the game performs consistently across
different devices, platforms, and configurations.

title: Functional Testing
meaning:
Functional Testing Deep Dive
What is Functional Testing?
Functional testing verifies that every game feature, mechanic, and
system operates correctly according to design specifications.
Testers systematically check that buttons work, physics behave
properly, progression systems function, and game rules are
enforced accurately.
Common Functional Bugs:
• Collision Detection Failure: Players can walk through walls or
fall through the floor due to broken collision boundaries.
• Save/Load Corruption: Game progress fails to save correctly,
or loading a save file crashes the game or resets player data.

title: UI and UX Testing
meaning:
UI/UX Testing Essentials
What is UI/UX Testing?
UI/UX testing evaluates the visual interface and user experience to ensure players can navigate menus intuitively, read text clearly,
and interact with the game comfortably. It focuses on usability, accessibility, and visual polish.
Example: Text Cutoff
Menu text or subtitles are partially hidden or truncated on
certain screen resolutions or aspect ratios, making content
unreadable.
Example: Button Overlap
UI buttons overlap each other in specific languages or
device sizes, making them impossible to click or causing
wrong inputs.

title: Playtesting for Engagement
meaning:
Playtesting for Engagement
Fun Factor
Is the game genuinely enjoyable? Does
it create memorable moments and
keep players wanting more?
Balance & Pacing
Are difficulty spikes fair? Does the
game maintain good rhythm without
feeling too slow or overwhelming?
Difficulty Curve
Does challenge increase smoothly? Are
tutorials effective and does
progression feel rewarding throughout?
Playtesting focuses on the subjective player experience—what feels right, what's frustrating, and what makes the game
worth playing. This feedback shapes design iterations and helps developers refine gameplay to be as compelling as
possible.

title: Compatibility Testing
meaning:
Compatibility Testing Coverage
Modern games must run smoothly across an incredible variety of hardware and software configurations.
Compatibility testing ensures consistent performance and quality no matter how players access your game.
Device Variations
Testing across different hardware specs: high-end gaming PCs, mid-range laptops, mobile devices, and older
systems.
OS Versions
Verifying compatibility with Windows 10/11, macOS versions, iOS, Android, PlayStation OS, Xbox OS, and Switch
firmware.
Resolutions & Displays
Ensuring proper rendering at 1080p, 1440p, 4K, ultrawide formats, and various aspect ratios without distortion.
Performance Issues
Monitoring frame rates, load times, memory usage, and identifying optimization opportunities for smooth
gameplay.

title: The Role of a Game Tester
summary: Session 1 ? The Role of a Game Tester
meaning:
The Role of a Game Tester
Key Responsibilities
• Execute test plans and document bugs clearly with
reproduction steps
• Verify fixes and conduct regression testing
• Communicate findings effectively to development
teams
• Maintain attention to detail while testing repetitively
• Provide constructive feedback on gameplay and user
experience
Session Takeaways
• QA is essential throughout the entire development
pipeline
• Different testing types serve specific quality goals
• Early bug detection saves time, money, and reputation
• Testers bridge the gap between developers and players
• Quality testing requires both technical skill and player
empathy
Ready to start your game testing journey? Apply these foundations, stay curious, and remember: every bug you
catch makes games better for millions of players.

title: Spotting Bugs in Mobile Games
summary: Session 2 ? Spotting Bugs in Mobile Games
meaning:
How to Spot Bugs in Mobile
Games
Visual Anomalies
• Graphics glitches or missing
textures
• UI elements overlapping or
misaligned
• Animation stuttering or
freezing
• Incorrect colours or visual
effects
Functional Issues
• Controls not responding as
expected
• Game logic errors or broken
mechanics
• Crashes or unexpected app
closures
• Performance problems like
lag or frame drops

title: Key Testing Strategies
meaning:
Key Testing Strategies
Exploratory Testing
Play the game naturally whilst staying
alert to unexpected behaviour or visual
inconsistencies
Edge Case Testing
Test boundary conditions like
minimum/maximum values, poor
connectivity, or device limitations
Regression Testing
Verify that previously working features
still function correctly after updates or
changes

title: Anatomy of a Bug Report
summary: Session 2 ? Anatomy of a Bug Report
meaning:
Anatomy of an Excellent Bug Report
Every effective bug report contains six essential components that enable developers to quickly understand and resolve issues
Clear Title
Concise summary of the issue
Reproduction Steps
Detailed sequence to recreate
Expected vs Actual
What should happen vs what does
Environment Details
Device, OS, and app version
Visual Evidence
Screenshots or video recordings
Severity Level
Impact on user experience

title: Writing an Effective Bug Title
summary: Session 2 ? Writing an Effective Bug Title
meaning:
Writing an Effective Bug Title
Poor Example
"Game doesn't work"
Too vague – provides no actionable information about
the specific issue or where it occurs
✓ Good Example
"Level 3 crashes when collecting power-up on
Samsung Galaxy S21"
Specific, clear, and includes key context about location
and device
Pro tip: Your title should enable someone to understand the core issue in under five seconds

title: Steps to Reproduce
meaning:
Steps to Reproduce
Clear reproduction steps are the most critical part of any bug report. Write them as if explaining to someone who has never used the app before.
Step 1
Launch PlayzHub app v2.1.0 on Android device
Step 2
Navigate to "Puzzle Games" category and select "Block Breaker"
Step 3
Complete Level 2 and proceed to Level 3
Step 4
Collect the yellow power-up in top-right corner
Result
Application crashes immediately to home screen

title: Expected and Actual Results
meaning:
Expected vs Actual Results
Expected Result
Collecting the yellow power-up should activate a shield
effect around the player's character for 10 seconds,
accompanied by a sound effect and visual animation.
The game should continue normally with the shield active.
Actual Result
Upon touching the yellow power-up, the app freezes for
approximately 2 seconds, displays a black screen, then
crashes completely to the device home screen.
No error message is shown.
This comparison clearly shows the gap between intended behaviour and what actually occurs, helping developers pinpoint
the root cause.
